title: Smooth SNC and absolute and relative projectivity for semilinearly induced finite families
statement: Let $e$ be a field [def-weil-field], $I$ a nonempty finite set, and $B=\coprod_{i\in I}B_i$ a finite disjoint union of integral proper finite-type $e$-schemes [def-pc-integral-scheme] [def-weil-proper-morphism] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Give effective Cartier divisors $C_i$ on $B_i$ [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal], and write $C=\coprod_i C_i$. For each $i$, let $F_i/e$ be a finite field extension [def-pc-field-extension] [def-pc-field-tower], let a finite group $J_i$ act on $F_i$ by $e$-automorphisms, and let $S_i$ be an integral smooth projective $F_i$-scheme with compatible semilinear $J_i$-action [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] [def-kun-projective]. Let $v_i:S_i\to B_i$ be an invariant surjective $e$-morphism, sending its generic point to that of $B_i$ with finite residue-field extension [def-weil-surjective-morphism] [def-sc-generic-point] [def-weil-residue-field]. Assume $D_i=(v_i^{-1}C_i)_{\rm red}$ is relative strict normal crossings over $F_i$ [def-trf-smooth-strict-normal-crossings-divisor]. Let $K/e$ be a finite normal extension, meaning every irreducible polynomial over $e$ with a root in $K$ splits in $K$, with embeddings $F_i\hookrightarrow K$, and let $G$ be a finite group acting on $K$ by $e$-automorphisms. Give subgroups $\Gamma_i\leq G$ and surjections $\Gamma_i\to J_i$ such that the two actions on $F_i$ agree. Form $W_i=S_i\times_{F_i}K$ with the diagonal $\Gamma_i$-action [def-pc-fibre-product], and $Y_i=G\times^{\Gamma_i}W_i$, the disjoint union of the copies of $W_i$ indexed by left cosets, where $(g\gamma,w)\sim(g,\gamma w)$ and the scalar structure of the copy $g$ is twisted by $g$ on $K$. Put $Y=\coprod_iY_i$, with the left $G$-action, and define $h:Y\to B$ by $[g,w]\mapsto v_i(\operatorname{pr}_1w)$. Then $Y$ is smooth and geometrically reduced over $K$ [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], is reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme], is projective over $K$, and is also projective over $e$, with projective meaning a closed immersion into finite-dimensional projective space. The morphism $h$ is projective in both the finite-projective-space and projective-bundle conventions [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism], and is surjective. The divisor $(h^{-1}C)_{\rm red}$ is relative strict normal crossings over $K$: it is reduced effective Cartier, and every intersection of $r$ distinct integral components is empty or smooth over $K$ of pure codimension $r$, also for $r=0$. No separability of $K/e$ or $F_i/e$ is assumed; empty divisors and unequal dimensions of the $B_i$ are allowed.

proof.text: Choose one representative of each left coset $G/\Gamma_i$, choosing $1$ for the identity coset. By the defining relation, each summand is a copy of $W_i$ with its scalar map twisted by an $e$-automorphism of $K$. Changing a representative from $g$ to $g\gamma$ changes the coordinate by $\gamma$, and $v_i\operatorname{pr}_1(\gamma w)=v_i\operatorname{pr}_1(w)$ by invariance. Thus the displayed maps glue to the stated invariant $e$-morphism $h$. A twisted copy is a base change along the corresponding automorphism of $\operatorname{Spec}K$, since that automorphism is invertible.

source.place: X 2.3 Step 2, contracted product and diagram (2.b), p.150.

proof.text: First $S_i/F_i$ is proper by projective-implies-proper, hence finite type by the definition of properness. For every $i$ apply relative SNC field-extension permanence to $S_i/F_i$, $D_i$ and $K/F_i$. It gives smoothness of $W_i/K$ and the relative SNC divisor $(D_i)_K$. Apply the same lemma to each scalar twist over the automorphism of $K$. The finite coproduct is smooth by the smooth-coproduct lemma. A smooth scheme over a field is geometrically reduced, and taking the trivial field extension also makes $Y$ reduced.

source.place: X 2.1 relative SNC definition p.149 and X 2.3 Step 2 pp.150--151; Stacks Tags 01VB and 056T.

proof.text: On an affine chart of $S_i$ let $I$ define $v_i^{-1}C_i$ and $J=\sqrt I$ define $D_i$. After any scalar change $A\to A\otimes_{F_i}K$, the extended ideals have the same radical: $I\subseteq J$, and every element of $J$ has a power in $I$, so the ideal generated by its image is nil modulo the extended $I$. Since $(D_i)_K$ is reduced by the preceding lemma, its ideal is precisely this radical. Thus the reduced inverse image of $C_i$ on a coset copy is the corresponding twist of $(D_i)_K$. On a disjoint union the divisor ideals glue componentwise; their local generators are nonzerodivisors on the same open summands. Components in different summands have empty intersection. In one summand the cited scalar-extension lemma gives all intersections and their pure codimensions, including $r=0$. Therefore $(h^{-1}C)_{\rm red}$ is relative SNC on $Y/K$.

source.place: X 2.3 Step 2 pp.150--151: reduced inverse image of the boundary on the induced copies; affine ideal calculation supplied by Q119.

proof.text: Choose the given closed immersion $S_i\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^{n_i}_{F_i}$. Base change of a closed immersion and the projective-space Cartesian square give $W_i\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^{n_i}_K$. The same argument along an automorphism of $K$ gives a finite-projective-space embedding for every twisted coset copy.

source.place: X 2.3 Step 2 p.150; Stacks morphisms.tex Tag 01WF (lemma-H-projective-base-change).

proof.text: Enumerate the finitely many coset summands as $Z_1,\ldots,Z_t$ and choose embeddings $Z_a\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^{n_a}_K$. In $\mathbf P^N_K$, where $N+1=\sum_a(n_a+1)$, use separate coordinate blocks for these projective spaces. Their images are closed and pairwise disjoint: the equations set all other blocks equal to zero, and two different blocks cannot both contain a projective point. The resulting map $\coprod_a Z_a\to\mathbf P^N_K$ is a closed immersion: on each standard affine coordinate chart only its own block meets the image, and there it is the given closed immersion followed by setting the other coordinates to zero. These charts cover the target. This proves $Y/K$ projective without any equality of dimensions.

source.place: X 2.3 Step 2 pp.150--151; explicit finite disjoint-union projective embedding supplied by Q119.

proof.text: The morphism $\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}e$ is finite, since $K$ has a finite $e$-basis. Hence it is projective in the bundle convention. The sheaf $\mathcal O$ on $\operatorname{Spec}e$ is ample: its section $1$ has affine nonvanishing locus equal to this one-point scheme. The projective-over-ample-base lemma makes $\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}e$ H-projective. Compose it with the H-projective map $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ to obtain the asserted finite-projective-space embedding over $e$.

source.place: X 2.3 Step 2 pp.150--151; Stacks Tags 0B3I, 087S, 01WE, with the elementary affine ampleness verification.

proof.text: Finite repeated application of the proper-coproduct lemma makes $B=\coprod_i B_i$ proper over $e$, hence separated. Apply H-projective permanence to $Y\xrightarrow{h}B\to\operatorname{Spec}e$: its composite is H-projective by Step 6, so $h$ is H-projective. In the closed-graph construction this is the embedding $(j,h):Y\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^M_e\times_e B=\mathbf P^M_B$, where $j$ is the embedding of Step 6. The canonical identification of this last projective space with the projective bundle of $\mathcal O_B^{M+1}$ makes the same embedding projective in the bundle convention.

source.place: X 2.3 Step 2 pp.150--151; Stacks Tag 0C4Q (lemma-projective-permanence), H-projective closed-graph proof, and projective space as the bundle of a finite free module.

proof.text: The map $\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}F_i$ is surjective, and its base change $W_i\to S_i$ is surjective. In the identity coset the restriction of $h$ is its composite with the given surjection $v_i:S_i\to B_i$, so it covers $B_i$. These images, for all $i$, cover $B$. Thus $h$ is surjective. No step has required a separable constant extension, a nonempty boundary, or a common dimension for different $B_i$.
